q1.answer: No. ADR013 (use node-fetch) is marked superseded in its own text and no longer applies. It was replaced by ADR014, which says frontend plugins and packages should prefer the fetchApiRef (which wraps fetch, injected via useApi), while Node.js code should use native fetch instead of node-fetch.

q2.answer: ADR007 requires all fetch/XMLHttpRequest calls in tests to be mocked with msw. It says doing so avoids each test having its own ad-hoc implementation of mocking network requests, i.e. it avoids inconsistent, per-test mocking approaches scattered across the codebase (unit tests through e2e tests each reinventing their own mocking).

q3.answer: ADR006 cites two problems: React.FC implicitly added a `children` prop to every component, and it did not support generic types on children. The ADR notes that Facebook removed React.FC from the official create-react-app TypeScript template because it was found to be an unnecessary feature with next to no benefit and these downsides.

q4.answer: ADR010 mandates Luxon and names Moment.js as the library it replaces, for two reasons: Moment.js suffers from large bundle sizes and mutable-state issues, and the Moment.js project itself was being sunset/is in maintenance mode, recommending users move to more modern alternatives.

q5.answer: ADR004 (Module Export Structure) requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files down to the package's root src/index.ts. It was meant to make it easy to answer the question "is this export in this module also exported by the package?" (equivalently, "what is exported from this directory?").

q6.answer: No, under ADR004's rule they are not part of the public API: the rule says a symbol is only exported from the package if every index file on the path from it up to the root re-exports the previous level, and there is no src/utils/index.ts and src/index.ts doesn't mention these files, so the chain to the root is broken — nothing needs to be explicitly marked private because the absence of a traceable index-file chain itself means 'not publicly exported'.

q7.answer: ADR011 says an x-react package is for shared widgets, hooks and similar code that both the plugin itself (x) and third-party frontend plugins can depend on; it would only become justified once other third-party frontend plugins need to reuse notifications' components/hooks, i.e. once there's cross-plugin shared frontend code to extract, which isn't currently the case for this single-package plugin.

q8.answer: ADR003 allows a default export only when 'absolutely necessary,' citing React.lazy modules as the example (React.lazy requires a module with a default export). For teams wanting to avoid even that, the ADR gives the workaround of wrapping the dynamic import and remapping the named export to `default` inline, e.g. `React.lazy(() => import('../path/to/Component').then(m => ({ default: m.Component })))`.

q9.answer: ADR015 defines the loader/component option pattern. Its Consequences section says it will be applied to update all APIs for the new frontend system (@backstage/frontend-* packages), but explicitly states existing APIs for the old frontend system (@backstage/core-* packages) will NOT be updated — so no, the team will not retrofit it onto pre-existing dev-app-style code.
